change: Moved Lower Back (Erector Spinae) from primary to secondary. In a front squat the upright torso position means Erector Spinae acts as a stabilizer rather than a prime mover; Quads and Glutes are the true drivers. EMG research shows no significant difference in erector spinae activation vs back squat, but the quad-dominant nature of the front squat makes it inappropriate as primary. Hamstrings (secondary) retained per squat protocol.
Added Lower Traps to the mid back primary entry (was only Upper Traps + Rhomboids). The full trapezius including lower fibers is activated during the shrug phase of the clean pull. No other changes.

Added Adductors as a secondary entry. The Coan deadlift uses a semi-sumo (wider) stance which distinctively engages adductors for hip stability and force production — confirmed by sumo/semi-sumo deadlift biomechanics research. Also added Lower Traps to the mid back secondary entry (was only Upper Traps + Rhomboids) since all trap fibers contribute to scapular stability in the deadlift lockout.

Added Anterior Deltoids to the shoulders primary entry. The high pull component involves forward arm drive / elbow abduction which recruits anterior deltoids alongside lateral and posterior deltoids. Also added Lower Traps to mid back primary entry (was only Upper Traps + Rhomboids) since lower traps are activated during the full shrug and pull phases of this explosive movement.

No changes. Muscle encoding, category, equipment, and trackingMode all verified correct. Lower abs primary with Rectus Femoris (hip flexor quad) primary is appropriate; obliques, adductors, and abductors as secondary match the circular leg motion mechanics.
